thread:
sam: Quick report 1: after the mkdocs->docusaurus migration a handful of fragment links under /guides/installer and /guides/cluster resolve to top-of-page instead of the header. Seeing support tickets and CI linkcheck warnings.
eli: Any concrete examples?
sam: /guides/installer#service-accounts and /guides/cluster#autoscaling. Clicking the deep link lands at the top.
rachel: I inspected the generated HTML. Some headings were wrapped in our custom <Note> MDX component during migration which changed slug computation. Also a few headings ended up as indented code blocks because of bad conversion, so no slug is produced.
infra-bot: linkcheck: nightly run found 6 broken fragments in build 4360. Report: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/4360/linkcheck
eli: Two-track fix: (1) add explicit heading ids on high-traffic pages, e.g. `## Service accounts {#service-accounts}`; (2) generate a redirects.json mapping old-fragment -> new-fragment for external links (blog posts, emails).
sam: For indented headings we have to edit content (unindent). Redirects won't help if the heading doesn't exist.
rachel: I'll run `rg "^\s{4,}#{1,6} " docs | sed -n '1,200p'` to find indented headings and open a small PR with fixes for installer/cluster.
eli: I'll prototype a slugmap generator that scans git history for previous heading slugs, diffs to current slugs, and emits a redirects map consumable by Docusaurus.
sam: Also add a minimal linkcheck unit test in `.github/workflows/linkcheck.yml` asserting known anchors exist post-merge. That prevents regressions.
infra-bot: Reminder: nightly rebuild at 02:00 UTC will re-run linkcheck after merges.
rachel: PR incoming with manual fixes and explicit ids. eli: ping when slugmap PR is ready and I'll fold in redirects before we flip on strict linkcheck.
